name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah is a male figure noted for his role in the restoration of Jerusalem, specifically for repairing a section of the city wall as recorded in Nehemiah 3:29. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional notes beyond this contribution to the rebuilding effort.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name emphasizes God's attentiveness, though it was not given directly by God according to the record in Nehemiah 3:29.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Shemaiah had a son named Shecaniah, as noted in Nehemiah 3:29. Beyond this explicit relationship, no other family connections are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his active participation in the physical and spiritual restoration of Jerusalem following the exile. By repairing the city wall, he contributed to the protection and reestablishment of the community under God's providence. His work symbolizes faithful obedience and commitment to God's covenant people during a pivotal time of rebuilding.
